lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Edge is going dull. Ten more swings, then I sharpen.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Large axe. Half the swings of the small one. Worth every gram of it.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Running the saw, boss. Don't bother talking to me till it's off.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Hand signals while the saw's going. Thumb up means I'm done.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: File, two strokes per tooth. Same count every time.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Rack's empty, chief. Order another axe on the camper computer, or I'm cutting with my teeth.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Priya, your edge is rolled. Look, there, along the bevel.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Wet handle. Choke up and keep your grip dry.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Decent gloves. Blisters stopped on day three. I'm grateful, and I don't say that often.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Report, boss: the big axe is near doubling my count. Best money the company's spent out here.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Tomas's swing is tighter than last week. Less wasted wood in his chips.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Chain's stretched. Tension it now or throw it later.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Best tool on this island, boss? A sharp edge and somebody who keeps it that way.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Twenty years in and still getting faster. Don't tell the young ones.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Helmet on, {listener}. Branches don't give warnings.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Saw doesn't mind the rain. I do.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Good boots. Wet slope and not one slip. Money well spent.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Small axe today, boss. Slower, but it never runs out of fuel.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Wiping the blade before we go in. Rust works overtime.

lines.speaker: EMP-01
lines.text: Choke off once it coughs. Pull hard, not long. There you go.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Big axe, big man. Nature's way, mate.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: This little axe is like eating soup with a teaspoon, mate.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Saw's going. Can't hear a word anyone says. Bliss.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Saw's doing the hard bit, mate. I'm just the bloke holding the pointy end away from me.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: No axe on the rack, mate. I'll carry, but I can't cut with my sunny smile.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: New gloves, mate. My hands haven't been this pampered since, well, never.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Marta's got that big axe sharp enough to slice bread. I'd know, I've thought about it.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Handle's worn smooth where my hand goes. We're getting to know each other.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Parcel locker's got something in it, mate. Hope it's biscuits. The human kind.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Can the camper computer order a pie, mate? Asking for a friend. The friend is me.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Helmet's a bit snug. My head's bigger than the company planned for.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Chainsaw in the rain. Loud, wet, and smells like a fuel can's packed lunch.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Big axe through a root. Like cutting a crusty loaf, that.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Swear I'm getting better at this, mate. Two swings fewer a tree, near enough.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Boots are earning their keep today, mate. Mud to the ankles and my socks still dry.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Biscuit, back off from the saw. You're not a log, even if you're shaped like one.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Swap you axes, mate? Yours looks lighter. Mine looks like a responsibility.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Tool rack's sorted, mate. Hung everything back up. Biscuit helped by sitting on the gloves.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: No tool today. Just these arms. They'll do.

lines.speaker: EMP-02
lines.text: Ears? I thought the ringing was just me being happy.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The large axe takes about forty percent fewer swings than the small one. I've been counting.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Too loud to hear anything. I watch the chips instead. They tell you plenty.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Report, boss: the saw chain will need replacing soon. The cuts are drifting to the left.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Helmets on, please. There's a hung branch two trees over.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Do the parts and the food come from the same supplier, boss? The parcel labels match.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: My strikes are landing closer together. Less chopping, more cutting.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Kickback comes off the top of the bar tip. Keep it away from knots.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: There's no tool for me on the rack, boss. Could we order one on the camper computer?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Oiled the axe heads. Two had rust at the eye, where the rain gets in.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Your strokes are much more even now. Did Marta show you that?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Wet gloves lose grip at the end of the swing. A second pair would be worth it.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: These boots have a deeper tread than the old ones. Fewer slips on the slope.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The large axe tires the shoulders by dusk. My accuracy drops after about six hours.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Dale, the saw is louder than standing next to a running truck. Are your ears covered?

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Dry wood makes finer sawdust. The air filter will need cleaning tonight.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Sawing, boss. Faster than the axe, but I can't hear anyone, so I keep looking up.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: The parcel locker light is on. Something's arrived from the supplier.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Small axe. More swings, but I can place every one exactly.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: My felling times are down by a third since the first week. I keep a record.

lines.speaker: EMP-03
lines.text: Oh. You're right. I'll hone it at lunch, if you'll show me the angle.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: The saw's so loud. I'll just nod at everyone.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Marta, could you show me how to start the saw? Sorry. It keeps flooding.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: The big axe is heavy. But it feels a bit like driving a truck instead of a van.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Small axe, boss. It's fine. It's actually fine. I'm used to it.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Sorry, boss, there's nothing on the rack for me. Is that okay? I can carry instead.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Helmet on. Ana made me promise. I promised.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Something in the parcel locker. I hope it's mine. Nothing's ever mine, actually. Never mind.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I can split a section in four swings now. It used to be seven.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: These boots grip like good tyres. I could go anywhere in these.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: The truck is my favourite tool. Is a truck a tool? I'm saying it's a tool.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Report, boss: I think I've improved with the axe. Fewer swings per section. Sorry, is that a report?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Turning the saw off now. I want to hear what's around us before dark.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Are your gloves stiff too? Mine are crunchy from all the sap.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Wet handle. Sorry, axe. I'll hold you properly.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: I put all the tools back on the rack. Sorted by size. Is that okay?

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Does the camper computer list trucks, boss? Just looking. Not asking. Mostly not asking.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Big axe on a section, and it just goes. That's nice.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Saw off for a second. Sorry. Just checking the top isn't swaying.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Twenty days with this small axe. I've given it a name. Don't tell Dale.

lines.speaker: EMP-04
lines.text: Oh. Oh no. Sorry. That explains a lot, actually.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Small axe, small grievances. Gets there in the end.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Chainsaw's like a packed bar on a Friday. Can't hear a word, so smile and nod.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Ordered anything nice on the camper computer, boss-love? Cushions? A kettle that whistles?

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Big axe today, boss-love. I feel like the lumberjack off a shortbread tin.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Nothing on the rack, boss-love. I can tend the fire, but I can't fell a tree with a ladle.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Helmet's not optional, sunshine. I've seen what a falling branch does to a hairdo.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Tomas, love, your gloves are on the wrong hands. Thumbs go on the inside.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Parcel locker's blinking. Either it's our gear, or the company's sent another form.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Wet gloves. Like doing the washing up in mittens.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Priya's chopping like she was born to it now. Remember her first day? Bless her.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: This big axe is heavier than a full keg. Twice as useful, too.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Good boots, these. Twenty years behind a bar, and my feet never had it so good.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: I'll signal when I'm done, love. Two waves means stop sawing, not hello.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Getting quicker with this axe. Who knew I had hidden talents? Besides cocktails.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Report, boss-love: tools are sharp, the rack's tidy, and Dale hasn't lost a glove all week.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Dust everywhere off this saw. My hair's going to smell of sawdust for a week.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Heard the supplier charges the company double for helmets. Can't say I mind.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Axes on the rack before dark, love. A tidy rack's a happy camp.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: Fifteen days in and I can start the saw on the first pull. Mostly.

lines.speaker: EMP-05
lines.text: You'd manage, love. I've seen what you do with a teaspoon and a jar of jam.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Starting the saw! Step back.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Too loud to talk. Wave if you need me.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Big axe makes short work of it.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Small axe. Patience, and a lot more swings.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: No tool left on the rack. Someone needs to order more.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Sharpening while there's light. A dull axe is a dangerous axe.

lines.speaker: trait:stronger
lines.text: Give me the heaviest axe there is. I'll keep it swinging all day.

lines.speaker: trait:hard_working
lines.text: Quick hone and back to it. Sharp edges, quicker trees.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: That chain's throwing dust, not chips. It needs sharpening.

lines.speaker: trait:level_headed
lines.text: Let the saw do the work. Don't lean on it.

lines.speaker: trait:timid
lines.text: The saw makes me jump every time it starts. Sorry.

lines.speaker: trait:sociable
lines.text: Swap stories while we hone the axes? Makes the time go quicker.

lines.speaker: trait:skeptical
lines.text: Can't hear a thing over this, so there's no point worrying about noises.

lines.speaker: trait:reliable_driver
lines.text: Tools strapped down in the truck bed. Nothing rattling loose.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Helmet on before you go under that crown.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Good tread on these boots. The mud's not winning today.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Sap's glued my gloves stiff. Still better than bare hands.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: I need a tool, boss. The camper computer can order one from the supplier.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Getting the hang of this. Fewer swings than last week.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Parcel locker's full. New gear from the supplier, I hope.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Wet chain flinging bark everywhere. Keep your visor down.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Killing the saw. Dusk is coming and I want my ears back.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Ten days with the big axe. I'd never go back to the small one.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Dry wood bites clean. The edge is holding up today.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: On the saw, boss. Can't hear you, but I can see you're there.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Wind's dropping twigs on my helmet. Glad I'm wearing it.

lines.speaker: trait:observant
lines.text: One axe on the rack has a cracked handle. I'm setting it aside.

lines.speaker: any
lines.text: Go on, then. You start, I'll keep the angle.
